Read the documents that fired on an item

inspect_cases.Rd

Pulls the documents that endorsed an item, with their full text, for checking whether the model was right.

Usage

inspect_cases(
  results,
  item,
  docs = NULL,
  ...,
  text = NULL,
  id = NULL,
  which = c("endorsed", "uncertain"),
  target = NULL,
  n = 6L,
  chars = NULL,
  file = NULL,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

results

A fathom_results object from measure() or read_checkpoints().

item

A string naming the item to inspect.

docs

A character vector of documents, or the data frame passed to measure(). Optional when measure() was given a character vector, since the documents are stored on the results in that case. Default is NULL.

...

Not used, and refused if anything reaches it. Every argument after it is name-only, so a misspelling lands here rather than being matched by position.

text, id

Strings naming the text and identifier columns, if docs is a data frame. text is then required, and id defaults to the row position.

which

A string choosing the documents, "endorsed" (the default) for those where target won or "uncertain" for the closest calls regardless of answer. "uncertain" has nothing to sort on when every document came back at the same extreme, and says so rather than returning corpus order under that label. To read the documents an item did not fire on, ask for the other label as target rather than for the complement of this one.

target

A string naming the label counted as endorsement. Defaults to the first.

n

An integer giving the number of documents to show. Default is 6.

chars

An integer giving the characters each document is truncated to, or NULL (the default) for full text. Warns.

file

A string giving a path to write markdown to instead of printing, or NULL (the default) to print.

seed

An integer giving a seed for the sample, or NULL (the default). It reaches this draw only, and the session's random stream is put back afterwards.

Value

Invisibly, a tibble of the selected cases, one row per document, in the order they are printed. Printing is the point of this function and the returned object is a convenience, so it carries the columns the printout drew on rather than a curated set.

  • id is the document identifier.

  • item is the item inspected, the same value on every row.

  • label is target, the same value on every row, since the rows for other labels are dropped before selection.

  • prob_renorm is the probability on target for that document, rescaled over the labels. This is what which filtered on and what the printout shows.

  • prob_other is the probability the model placed on tokens that were none of the labels, for that document.

  • text is the document, joined from docs. Truncated if chars was set. Named text even when the source column was called something else.

Any other columns the results carry travel through untouched, including anything passed to keep in measure() and the remaining diagnostic columns. A run that found no qualifying cases returns a tibble with no rows.

The header line

Three numbers, in this order. How many cases are printed, how many qualified before sampling down to n, and how large the corpus was. The middle one is the one to read, since it says whether the printed cases are all of them or a sample. Reporting the corpus size alone would read as though every document not shown had failed the filter, which is the opposite of what it means.

Endorsement by label count

On two labels it is the 0.5 cut on prob_renorm, which is what item_report() counts as endorse_renorm. Above two the labels compete for one pool, a winner at 0.3 clears no cut, and endorsement is instead the label that took the most mass, which is what item_report() counts as n_won.

"uncertain" is a rank rather than a threshold in both cases, so it commits to no cut point. On two labels it sorts by distance from 0.5. Above two it sorts by margin, the gap between the winning label and the runner-up, so the first rows are the closest calls.

Excerpts versus full text

Full text is the default. The passage that triggered an item is often outside a keyword-centered window, so an excerpt can read as a false negative when the item was working. Setting chars truncates and warns.

See also

item_report() for the summary these documents sit behind. coding_sample() for drawing cases to hand to a coder rather than reading a few.

Examples

# Results from a real run ship with the package, so this needs no server.
p <- system.file("extdata", "vignette_results.rds", package = "fathom")
baked <- readRDS(p)
res <- baked$res_six

# measure() was given a data frame, so the documents are passed again.
inspect_cases(res, "category", parlasent, text = "sentence", id = "id",
  target = "1", n = 2, seed = 1)
#> 
#> # category  (2 of 17 endorsed, from 100 documents)
#> 
#> **Question**
#> 
#> ```
#> Where does this sentence fall on the six-point sentiment scale?
#> 
#> 1 = entirely or predominantly negative
#> 2 = ambiguous, or a mixture of sentiments, leaning negative
#> 3 = no sentiment of its own, leaning negative
#> 4 = no sentiment of its own, leaning positive
#> 5 = ambiguous, or a mixture of sentiments, leaning positive
#> 6 = entirely or predominantly positive
#> ```
#> 
#> ---
#> 
#> **uk_017** | P(1) = 1.0000, other = 0.00e+00, 26 words
#> 
#> Apparent conflicting activities (where two announcements seem to contradict) and stating ambitious targets that are then not achieved were aligned to eroding trust with the public.” 
#> 
#> ---
#> 
#> **uk_040** | P(1) = 0.9834, other = 2.42e-07, 13 words
#> 
#> We know that the Government have paid £33 million to settle a lawsuit.
